newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes muted, market seeks direction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes muted, market seeks direction.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude trade was muted on Tuesday as the market sought direction amid a continuing slew of Iraqi news, traders said.
Baghdad submitted a new price formula to the United Nations for renewed exports, but traders said the levels were "too aggressive."

Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) submitted a price for U.S. buyers for Basrah Light crude of West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus $4.40 a barrel, 20 cents a barrel higher than the price it was at when oil was last lifted in May.
At least one trader said the price should be around $5.00 a barrel under WTI to account to rising freight rates.
Iraq is expected to submit new formulas by Wednesday, with liftings possible as early as this weekend, traders said.
Foreign crude trade was subdued as traders digested the latest chapter in the Iraqi saga.

A U.S. refiner was heard to have picked up a Nigerian Qua Iboe cargo on Monday from a Swiss trader at around $1.75-1.80 a barrel over Dated Brent on a delivered basis, but the deal could not be immediately confirmed.
At least three other cargoes of Qua Iboe are on offer for September arrival in the U.S. Gulf, with asking prices around Dated Brent plus $1.85 a barrel.

In Latin America, buyers and sellers were groping for direction in an increasingly volatile market for sweet Cusiana crude. Last Friday, a U.S. refiner bought a cargo for October WTI minus 78 cents, up 21 cents from the last deal a few days earlier.
Buyers seemed to be hanging back, with asking prices varying from minus 57 cents to minus 65 cents.
Elsewhere in the region, Peruvian state oil company Petroperu is seeking to buy 380,000 barrels of crude oil for August 29-31 arrival, a Latin American trade source said.
Offers are due August 6, with the award scheduled for August 7 on either an fob or cif basis.

Petroperu listed as possible candidates Colombia's Cano Limon, South Blend, Vasconia and Cusiana grades, Venezuela's Mesa, Lagotreco and Guafita, Ecuador's Oriente, Peru's Lote 8, Mexico's Isthmus, and Argentina's Rincon, Medanito and Escalante.
